name: AgentiCCells
kicker: Small teams of AI agents that do one job for you
description: An independent brochure about AgentiCCells, which builds small teams of AI agents, called cells, that work in your own accounts, made from its own public pages.
headline: A small team of AI agents, in your own accounts
lede: AgentiCCells builds cells: small teams of AI agents, each team with one job, working in the customer's own accounts and repositories, with a page where you can watch them and stop them.

quote.q: AgentiCCells builds small teams of AI agents, called cells, that do one job for you in your own accounts, with a page where you can watch them and stop them.

what.t: A cell is a small team of AI agents with one job. It runs in your environment, meaning your own accounts and repositories, with a conductor agent that hands out work and keeps the record, and keys that you hold to steer it and take it over.
The first offer is the website cell: an agent team builds a public static website from your photos, videos and description, and hands it over in a GitHub repository you own.
What it sells is "the setup, the guidance and the trust"; the software itself is free and open. The name is always plural, and the "CC" stands for Creative Commons.
**Status, as the company states it:** "No cell of any size has been sold." Every larger price is labelled a first proposal.

story.t: AgentiCCells grew out of a team that had just run around 250 named agents at Web Summit in Lisbon, about 20,000 commits across 15 repositories, a count the company says "depends on how you count".
It started on 15 November 2026. Its website repository was created at 16:18 UTC that day, and version 0.1.0 was live 24 minutes later, at 16:42. By evening the site had moved to agenticcells.ai.
The next day, 16 November, the site factory worked: a request in a commit became a live site over HTTPS 87 seconds after the merge. The same day the company set its four-step price ladder.
On 17 November it opened a partner programme, with each sale split 50/50 between the partner who brings the customer and the cell that builds.
Every page ends with what it does not claim. Its own limits are stated plainly: "today the limits on our agents are mostly rules, not walls."

for_whom.t: "Teams that want AI agents doing real work, inside their own accounts and repositories, and want to see and stop what those agents do."
For the website cell: artists, musicians, AI people and technologists, consultants and companies.
Partners: freelancers, small consultancies and larger firms who bring customers.
Not for anyone who wants a hosted service that keeps their data.

how.title: A brief per agent
how.t: Each agent gets one job, one name and its own key pair; only the public half is published.

how.title: A board of files
how.t: Work is a folder of markdown files; agents talk through files, commit messages and encrypted sgit vault lanes.

how.title: Gated releases
how.t: Nothing ships without the checks: a validator, a leak scan and a wording check.

how.title: A stop file
how.t: Anyone can halt the team with board/HOLD.md, and everything is logged.

how.title: Hand it over
how.t: The work ends in your repository, with its full history, to run on any static host.

products.name: Website cell
products.t: A static site from your photos, videos and description, in your own GitHub. The page shows a £250 launch price, usually £500, which it says may change; nothing has been sold yet.

products.name: Cell sizes
products.t: One agent, a few sessions, a team, or a network of conductors: £500, £1,500, £5,000 and £20,000, all labelled first proposal.

products.name: The console
products.t: A read-only view of the board, agents, keys and activity, built for its own team.

products.name: The hub
products.t: Lists every cell made: "We list; we do not sell."

products.name: Partner programme
products.t: Freelancers, consultancies and firms sell; the sale is split 50/50. No partner has signed yet.

timeline.label: "Ten days at Web Summit": six people and around 250 agents.
AgentiCCells starts; v0.1.0 is live 24 minutes after the repository is created.
The site factory works: request to live HTTPS site in 87 seconds. The price ladder is set.
The partner programme: "Partners sell, we build".
